role.altitude: The transportation planner keeps judging traffic effects, choosing scenarios, deciding what a plan needs and owning every number; pulling counts, calculating trips and parking, exporting model data and drafting standard chapters shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining calculators, export scripts and the reference library behind drafted text
role.ambitious_version: A planner who answers a developer's plan within a week with a traffic advice built on current counts.

tasks.short: Read development plans, calculate trips and parking demand, check traffic model effects, review development plans for transportation system effects, infrastructure requirements and compliance with regulations, and write the advice.

steps.what: Transportation planner reads the development plan and its traffic paragraph for floor areas, homes, parking and access points

loop.input: The development plan documents submitted by the developer.
loop.output: Homes by type, floor area by use, parking places and access points, each with the page it comes from.
loop.check: Every figure must quote its source text with page number, or it is left blank for the planner; figures that differ between documents are marked.
loop.why_not_simpler: Plans arrive as long PDFs in each developer's own layout.

steps.what: Transportation planner calculates trip generation and parking demand from the plan figures and the norms
Transportation planner checks the plan's effects on surrounding roads in the traffic model
Transportation planner reviews the effects, infrastructure requirements and compliance with applicable transportation regulations
Transportation planner writes the traffic advice to the project leader

tasks.design: A bounded step lifts homes, floor areas, parking places and access points from the developer's plan with page references. A calculator holds the municipality's parking norms and trip rates and computes trips and parking demand from those figures. The advice template takes the calculated tables, and the planner writes the conclusions. Checking network effects in the traffic model and judging compliance stay with the planner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were copied from PDFs into a fresh spreadsheet for each plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that extract figures with page references; norm tables in a shared calculator.
tasks.still_hard: Plans with mixed uses where norms overlap.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which junction will fail long before the model says so.

ambition.what: Advise on small plans that today get no traffic check.

tasks.altitude: Less copying and calculating; advice stays with the planner.

evidence.claim: A traffic modelling package is used for network models in transport planning.
A consultancy partly refunded a government report with fabricated references, so every extracted figure carries its page.

assumptions: Boundary: from the developer's plan to the traffic advice; negotiating with the developer is outside.
Input contract for s1: plan documents as searchable PDFs from the developer; scanned drawings are read by the planner.
Input contract for s2: the municipality's parking norms and trip rates loaded in the calculator by the planner and updated when policy changes.
Model checks, judgement and conclusions keep their full or nearly full time.
unknowns: Number of plans reviewed per month.
research_questions: How often do extracted figures differ from what the planner finds?

already_counted.description: Transportation planner checks marked and blank figures against the plan.

incremental.description: Transportation planner keeps norm tables in the calculator current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few large plans that need model work; high: many small plans with standard norms.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine the approvals or permits needed, collect drawings and studies, draft the traffic decision and application documents, fill in the application, have the final documents approved, submit them and answer the authority's questions.

steps.what: Transportation planner determines which approvals or permits the planned project needs
Transportation planner collects drawings, studies and data for the applications
Transportation planner prepares the necessary documents: the traffic decision text and its motivation

loop.input: The standard decision template, the measures from the project drawings and the conclusions of the traffic study.
loop.output: A draft motivation for the traffic decision in the template's sections.
loop.check: Every reason must cite a section of the traffic study or a drawing number, and the legal parts come only from the template, or the sentence is marked; the planner edits all text.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template holds the legal text; the motivation differs per project.

steps.what: Transportation planner fills in the permit application on the government portal
Department head approves the final decision and application
Transportation planner submits the approved application on the portal
Transportation planner answers questions from the permitting authority

approvals.approved_version: the decision and application as approved by the department head in s5; any change needs a new approval

tasks.design: A checklist by project type lists the approvals and permits usually needed and the documents each asks for, and the project folder is set up with those slots. The decision template holds the legal text, and a bounded step drafts the motivation from the traffic study and drawings, citing each source. Filling in the portal, the department head's approval, submitting and answering the authority stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each application started from an old example and a search for documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Document templates and models that draft text with cited sources.
tasks.still_hard: Projects that need several permits from different authorities.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the permitting officer will question.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and drafting; approvals stay with people.

reach.learn: Whether complete applications cut requests for more information.

evidence.claim: AI text that informs the public must be disclosed unless a person is responsible as editor; the planner edits and the department head approves.
A consultancy partly refunded a government report with fabricated references, so every reason in the draft must cite the study or a drawing.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and submitting the application; the authority's decision is outside.
Input contract for s1: the checklist by project type kept by the planning team.
Input contract for s3: the traffic study and drawings in the project folder; the decision template kept by the legal team.
Filling in, submitting and answering questions keep their full or nearly full time; the department head's approval is outside the planner's savings.
research_questions: Do requests for more information fall?

already_counted.description: Transportation planner edits the drafted motivation.

incremental.description: Transportation planner keeps the checklist by project type current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual projects with new permit types; high: repeat traffic decisions for standard measures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scope the assessment, export traffic data for noise and air models, review specialists' results, produce environmental documents such as the traffic chapter of an environmental assessment, and check references and consistency.

steps.what: Transportation planner scopes the environmental assessment with specialists and the competent authority
Transportation planner compiles traffic volumes per road section and vehicle type for the noise and air models
Transportation planner reviews the environmental specialists' noise and air results
Transportation planner produces the traffic chapter of the environmental document

loop.input: The fixed tables from the traffic model and the environmental input data, and the chapter outline.
loop.output: Draft text describing method, volumes and changes per scenario around the tables.
loop.check: Every number in the text must match a table cell, or the sentence is marked; no new references are added; the planner edits all text and writes the conclusions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables carry the numbers; the chapter must explain them in words.

steps.what: Transportation planner checks references and consistency of numbers across chapters

tasks.design: A versioned script exports traffic volumes per road section and vehicle type from the traffic model in the formats the noise and air specialists use. A bounded step drafts the descriptive text of the traffic chapter around the fixed tables, and a check script compares every number in the report with the model tables and every reference with the project library. Scoping, reviewing specialists' results and conclusions stay with the planner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volumes were reshaped by hand for each specialist and numbers checked by reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Scripted exports from traffic models, and checks that match report numbers to tables.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining why scenarios differ to a lay reader.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a model result is plausible for this town.
tasks.altitude: Less reshaping and checking; content stays with the planner.

reach.learn: Whether scripted input files cut rework.

evidence.claim: A traffic modelling package produces network volumes for planning studies.
A consultancy partly refunded a government report with fabricated references.
Public documents with AI text need disclosure unless a person is responsible as editor.

assumptions: Boundary: the traffic part of an environmental document; noise and air modelling are the specialists' work.
Input contract for s2: traffic model output per scenario, and the export script kept in version control by the planner; specialists agreed the file formats.
Input contract for s5: the project reference library kept by the planner.
Scoping and reviewing results keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of environmental documents per year.
research_questions: Do consistency errors found in review fall?

already_counted.description: Transportation planner edits drafted chapter text and fixes marked sentences.

incremental.description: Transportation planner maintains the export and check scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a single small project; high: large projects with many scenarios and several specialists.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather traffic counts, analyse data and run scenarios, prepare engineering studies or specifications, and review studies or specifications from consultants.

steps.what: Transportation planner gathers traffic counts and data for the study area
Transportation planner analyses the data and runs model scenarios
Transportation planner prepares the engineering study or specification text

loop.input: The scenario result tables and the study outline.
loop.output: Draft text for method and results sections around the tables.
loop.check: Every number must match a result table, or the sentence is marked; the planner writes conclusions and edits all text.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables carry the results; readers need them explained.

steps.what: Transportation planner reviews engineering studies or specifications from consultants

loop.output: A list of the assumptions, input data and design values used, each with its page.
loop.check: Every item must quote its source text with page number, or it is dropped; the planner judges each assumption.
loop.why_not_simpler: Assumptions are spread through long reports in each consultant's own layout.

tasks.design: A script pulls traffic counts and speeds for the study area from the national road traffic data portal and the municipality's own counters into one table. Scenarios still run in the traffic model under the planner's control. A bounded step drafts method and results text around the fixed tables, checked number by number, and lists the assumptions in consultants' studies with page references for the planner's review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were downloaded and combined by hand, and consultants' assumptions had to be found by reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Open national traffic data, scripted pulls and models that draft or extract with checks.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a consultant's assumption does not fit local behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Less data gathering and writing; analysis stays with the planner.

reach.learn: Whether a standard assumptions list speeds up review rounds.

evidence.claim: The national road traffic data portal publishes traffic data.
A traffic modelling package runs network scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and reviewing studies; decisions on projects are outside.

Input contract for s1: counts and speeds from the national road traffic data portal and the municipality's counters, pulled by a script the planner maintains; manual counts by consultants arrive as files and are added by hand (about a third).
Analysis and model runs keep most of their time.
unknowns: How many studies are prepared and reviewed per year.
research_questions: Do reviews catch more doubtful assumptions?

already_counted.description: Transportation planner checks pulled counts for gaps and faulty counters.

incremental.description: Transportation planner maintains the data pull script.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: studies built on new manual counts; high: studies on corridors covered by the national data portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
